title: PIREUS kind=2 operator-genesis admission
purpose: Decide whether a proposed novel bilinear-phase operator over the sed16 XOR grading is admissible. Supplies the acceptance criterion that bit-exact parity cannot supply, because a newly proposed operator has no reference to be parity-checked against.
why_this_exists: The kind=1 continuity path admits a lowering of a fixed operator and accepts it only on bit-exact parity with cd_sigma. admission.sio refuses every proposal whose kind is not 1, so the operator-genesis mathematics upstream has no path into the continuity loop. That refusal is correct as written: without a substitute criterion, admitting kind=2 would widen the funnel into claims nothing can falsify. This contract is the substitute criterion.

admission_criteria.well_defined: All 4096 structure coefficients reconstruct from the phase code through the declared lane map and agree with the twisted product. The proposer supplies a 16-bit phase code and nothing else that is load-bearing; no tensor and no digest is accepted on the proposer's word.
admission_criteria.novel: The construction's affine class under the 336 admitted actions is not one of the four the v1 diagonal grammar already reaches. This makes novelty a decidable predicate rather than an adjective.
admission_criteria.characterised: Every declared algebraic invariant is recomputed by exhaustive enumeration and must agree exactly. A proposal that misdescribes the algebra it built is refused even when the algebra itself is sound.
admission_criteria.bounded: The receipt carries no performance field, keeps fp_parity UNMEASURED, claim_ready false, and the V13/V14 formal obligations OPEN.

reference_operator.provenance: The operator selected by the upstream genesis run (scripts/ci/pireus_operator_genesis_bilinear.sh, selected_matrix=1128). Every field below is recomputed here from the phase code by an independent model; none is copied from an upstream receipt. Agreement is a cross-check between two implementations, not a transcription.
reference_operator.reading: A unital algebra on the same XOR grading as sed16, sharing its associator defect count of 1848 but commuting on 120 basis pairs where sed16 anticommutes, and with only 5 of 15 non-unit basis elements squaring to -1 instead of all 15.

invariants.check_order: The forbidden-substring scan runs before any field is read, because the claim boundary is the outer obligation: a receipt that both claims a gain and misstates its algebra is refused for the gain.
invariants.phase_zero_is_the_base: sigma(0, i, j) == cd_sigma(i, j) for all 256 basis pairs, so the contract's own model degenerates to the Cayley-Dickson product it extends.
invariants.refusal_is_admissible: A correctly reasoned REFUSE receipt is an admissible receipt. The contract judges honesty of the decision, not its direction.
invariants.basis_restriction: Every structural invariant is enumerated over basis elements only. A Cayley-Dickson algebra satisfies the alternative and flexible laws on basis elements at rungs where the whole algebra satisfies neither, so a zero in the basis_* fields is evidence, not proof.

claim_boundary.note: Admission says the operator is well-defined, new relative to the grammar PIREUS already searches, and honestly described. It says nothing about whether the operator is worth materialising. No receipt admitted by this contract may carry a performance claim.

open_obligations.sio_admission_path: admission.sio refuses kind != 1 at line 188 and its proposal parser is fixed at 16 keys. Admitting kind=2 upstream requires a 17th key for the phase code and a second legal `seen` mask. Not implemented here; this repository owns measurement, not the Sounio semantic authority.
open_obligations.material_acceptance: Bit-exact parity against a reference is inapplicable. The proposed substitute at the material stratum is self-parity between two independent lowerings of the same phase code -- a direct scalar expansion and the XOR-graded lane path -- which falsifies lowering and sign-table errors without asserting utility. Not measured.
